überraschen.et: über- + raschen, compare Low German overraschen, överraschen, English over-, rush. Compare also Middle Low German vorraschen, vörraschen (“to take by surprise”).

s: to talk over, to talk into, to persuade (implying that the person gives in, but is not inwardly convinced; unlike überzeugen)
Sie sollte eigentlich um zehn zu Hause sein, aber dann hat sie mich überredet, dass sie bis Mitternacht bleiben darf.
At first she was supposed to be home at ten, but then she persuaded me to let her stay until midnight.
überreden.et: From Middle High German überreden. Equivalent to über- (“over”) + reden (“talk”).

s: to hand something over, to present
Ich habe die Überreste einer untergegangenen Zivilisation gefunden.
I've found the remnants of a lost civilisation.
In diesem Tal fanden Forscher fossile Überreste von Dinosauriern.
Researchers found fossil remains of dinosaurs in this valley.
remains, leftover(s): non-traditional source (inadvertently produced source of information of historiographical interest)
to lap (complete a whole lap more than another racer)
Wenn ein Biathlet überrundet ist, wird er disqualifiziert.
When a biathlete has been lapped, he is disqualified.
to exceed by a large margin, to have an uncatchable lead over
Mit unserer neuen Technologie werden wir die Konkurrenz überrunden.
With our new technology we will outdistance the competition.
überrunden.et: From either über- (“over-”) + runden (“to make round”) or rather directly from the noun Runde (“round, lap”). The simplex verb has no really fitting sense, but compare umrunden (“to circle, move around”).

s: to run over (i.e. by a vehicle)
rollover protection structure, rollover protection system (ROPS)
blindsiding; the act of taking someone or something by surprise

überrinnen.et: From Middle High German überrinnen, from Old High German *ubarrinnan. Equivalent to über + rinnen.

s: to trickle over and across something or someone.
A shower of rain trickled over me.
